s: In which areas does financial inclusion particularly seek to expand banking infrastructure?
x: Inclusion extends services to the poor and expands banking in underserved and rural areas, not metros.

s: Who chaired the Committee on Comprehensive Financial Services for Small Businesses and Low-Income Households, which provided the basis for PMJDY and payments and small finance banks?
x: The Nachiket Mor Committee was constituted in 2013 and recommended comprehensive financial services, including a bank account for every household.

s: Who chaired the Chief Ministers' Committee on Digital Payments during 2016–17?
x: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu chaired the 2016–17 Chief Ministers' Committee on Digital Payments.

s: Which of the following committees is wrongly matched with its subject?
o: Ratan Watal Committee – microfinance sector after the AP crisis
Deepak Mohanty Committee – medium-term path on financial inclusion
Y.H. Malegam Committee – microfinance sector after the AP crisis
x: The Ratan Watal Committee dealt with digital payments; the microfinance sector after the AP crisis was the Malegam Committee's subject.

s: Which of the following is an objective of financial inclusion?
o: Restricting access to formal financial services
Limiting banking infrastructure to urban areas
x: Promoting financial literacy is an aim of financial inclusion, so people know about and use financial services. The other options are the reverse of inclusion.

s: Which of the following is NOT an aim or outcome of financial inclusion?
o: Access to credit for weaker sections
Payments and remittances through the formal system
x: Financial inclusion increases, not reduces, financial security; it eases formal payments and widens access to insurance and credit.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Financial Stability and Development Council – chaired by Dr. C. Rangarajan
Financial inclusion – access to formal financial services for the poor
Financial exclusion – lack of access to insurance and credit
Committee on Financial Inclusion (2006) – chaired by Dr. C. Rangarajan
x: The FSDC is chaired by the Union Finance Minister; Dr. C. Rangarajan chaired the 2006 Committee on Financial Inclusion.

s: Who chairs the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)?
x: The FSDC is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, not by Rangarajan.

s: With which subject did the Y.H. Malegam Committee (2010) of the RBI deal?
x: The Malegam Committee studied the microfinance sector after the AP crisis; digital payments was Watal and payments banks Nachiket Mor.

s: Who chaired the 2016 committee on digital payments set up by the Ministry of Finance?
x: The Ratan Watal Committee (2016, MoF) dealt with digital payments; Deepak Mohanty (2015) dealt with financial inclusion.

s: Which period does the RBI's National Strategy for Financial Inclusion cover?
x: The National Strategy for Financial Inclusion of the RBI covers 2019-24.

s: With which subject was the C. Rangarajan Committee of 2006-2008 concerned?
x: The Rangarajan Committee formed in 2006 (report January 2008) was the Committee on Financial Inclusion.

s: Which of the following pairs (committee – reform area) is correctly matched?
x: Nachiket Mor is linked to financial inclusion; Shanta Kumar to FCI/PDS, Kasturirangan to NEP 2020 and Urjit Patel to inflation targeting.

s: The National Mission for Financial Inclusion was announced on which date and formally launched on which date?
x: The National Mission for Financial Inclusion was announced on 15 August 2014 and launched on 28 August 2014.

s: What is the minimum balance required in a PMJDY basic savings bank deposit account?
x: PMJDY accounts are zero-balance accounts that earn interest and come with a RuPay debit card and DBT facility.

s: Up to what amount can PMJDY account holders get an overdraft?
x: The PMJDY overdraft limit is ₹10,000; the RuPay card carries ₹2 lakh accident cover.

s: PMJDY accounts may be linked with PMJJBY, PMSBY and which other scheme?
x: PMJDY accounts are linked with PMJJBY, PMSBY and the Atal Pension Yojana.

s: The three tenets of PMJDY are banking the unbanked, securing the unsecured and which other?
x: PMJDY's tenets are banking the unbanked, securing the unsecured and funding the unfunded.

s: About how many PMJDY accounts were there as of August 2026?
x: PMJDY accounts stood at 59.09 crore (19 Aug 2026), up from 14.72 crore in 2015; 45.95 crore are rural/semi-urban.

s: Women hold about what share of PMJDY accounts?
x: Women hold 32.92 crore of 59.09 crore accounts, over half; about three-fourths are rural/semi-urban.

s: What accident insurance cover does the RuPay debit card issued with a PMJDY account carry?
x: The PMJDY RuPay card carries ₹2 lakh accident cover; the life cover is ₹30,000.

s: The PMJDY overdraft is available after how many months of satisfactory account conduct?
x: The overdraft of up to ₹10,000 is given after 6 months of good conduct.

s: What is the main objective of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana?
o: A bank account for every household
x: PMJDY, the National Mission for Financial Inclusion launched on 28 August 2014, aims at a bank account for every household.

s: Which is the nodal department for the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana?
o: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
x: PMJDY is run by the Department of Financial Services of the Ministry of Finance.

s: What life insurance cover is given with a PMJDY account?
x: PMJDY gives a life cover of ₹30,000, besides ₹2 lakh accident cover on the RuPay debit card.

s: Through what does AePS, which supports financial inclusion and interoperable banking, enable basic banking transactions?
x: AePS (Aadhaar Enabled Payment System) lets people do basic banking just by Aadhaar authentication.

s: By whom was the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) set up in 2008?
o: RBI and the Indian Banks' Association
RBI and the State Bank of India
x: NPCI was set up in 2008 by the RBI and IBA as a not-for-profit company under the PSS Act, 2007.

s: What does '123Pay' refer to?
x: 123Pay brings UPI to feature phones; e-RUPI is the prepaid voucher, FASTag the RFID toll tool and IMPS the instant interbank transfer.

s:
Consider the following about NPCI:
1. It was incorporated in December 2008 as a not-for-profit company.
2. It was incorporated as a Section 8 company under the Companies Act, 1956.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: NPCI was set up in December 2008 as a not-for-profit Section 25 company under the 1956 Act; Section 8 is the matching provision of the 2013 Act.

s: With what is NETC, operated in India's payments system, associated?
x: NETC is FASTag toll collection; RuPay is the card network, UPI handles instant A2A payments and IMPS instant interbank transfers.

s: In which year was BHIM launched?
x: BHIM and NETC FASTag came in 2016; the PSS Act in 2007, AePS in 2010 and NACH in 2012.

s:
Arrange the following NPCI milestones in chronological order:

A. RuPay launched
B. UPI pilot
C. Authorisation for retail payment systems / NFS operations
D. IMPS introduced
x: The order is NFS operations and authorisation (2009), IMPS (2010), RuPay (2012) and the UPI pilot (2016). The answer is C, D, A, B.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Bharat BillPay is an interoperable bill-payment system; NACH handles bulk recurring payments, BHIM is a UPI app and the RBI is the regulator.

s: To which payment system does the minimum transaction amount of Rs 2 lakh apply?
x: The Rs 2 lakh minimum is for RTGS; NEFT has no minimum and settles in deferred net half-hourly batches.

s: Which payment system is described as the largest interoperable ATM network in India?
x: The National Financial Switch, or NFS, is the largest interoperable ATM network.

s: For what is NACH mainly used?
o: Bulk recurring payments such as salaries and dividends
x: NACH handles bulk recurring payments; tolls are NETC/FASTag, feature phones 123Pay and bills Bharat BillPay.

s: What is e-RUPI?
x: e-RUPI is a person- and purpose-specific prepaid voucher; the domestic card network is RuPay and NPCI's UPI app is BHIM.

s: Which body designed and launched the National Financial Switch (NFS) in 2004?
x: NFS was launched in 2004 by RBI's IDRBT; NPCI took it over in 2009.

s: Under which Act does NPCI function?
x: NPCI works under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 as the umbrella body for retail payments.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about RTGS and NEFT?
o: RTGS settles on a real-time gross basis
NEFT settles in half-hourly deferred net batches
x: RTGS has a minimum of ₹2 lakh; NEFT has no minimum.

s: In which year was the RuPay card launched by NPCI?
x: NPCI launched RuPay, India's domestic card network, in 2012.

s: Which organisation developed the BHIM app?
x: BHIM is NPCI's UPI app, launched in 2016; NPCI also runs RuPay, UPI and NFS.

s: Which of the following is India's domestic card payment network?
x: RuPay is NPCI's domestic card network that reduces dependence on Visa and Mastercard; NETC is for toll collection.

s: In which year were IMPS and AePS introduced by NPCI?
x: NPCI introduced IMPS (24x7 instant interbank transfer) and AePS in 2010.

s: For what is Bharat QR used?
o: An interoperable QR code payment acceptance solution
A digital rupee wallet of RBI
A credit rating for small merchants
x: Bharat QR, launched in February 2017, lets a customer scan one merchant QR code to pay instantly; it is the world's first interoperable QR code acceptance solution.

s: Which of the following developed Bharat QR, launched in February 2017?
x: Bharat QR was developed jointly by NPCI, Mastercard and Visa and launched on 20 February 2017.

s: What range of loans does the 'Kishore' category under MUDRA cover?
x: Shishu is up to ₹50,000, Kishore ₹50,001–₹5 lakh, Tarun ₹5–10 lakh and Tarun Plus ₹10–20 lakh.

s: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) was launched on which date?
x: PMMY was launched on 8 April 2015. MUDRA Ltd was established earlier, on 18 March 2015.

s: Of which institution is MUDRA Ltd, which refinances lenders under PMMY, a subsidiary?
x: MUDRA Ltd was set up as a subsidiary of SIDBI on 18 March 2015 to undertake refinance functions.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly associated with PMMY?
o: Loans restricted exclusively to large corporate enterprises
x: PMMY targets non-corporate, non-farm micro and small enterprises, not large corporate enterprises. Loans are collateral-free up to ₹20 lakh, supported by CGFMU guarantees, and linked with the MUDRA Card.

s: Which Union Ministry administers the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana?
o: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
Ministry of Finance through the Department of Financial Services
x: PMMY is run by the Ministry of Finance, specifically through the Department of Financial Services.

s: What range of loans does the Tarun Plus category under PMMY cover?
x: Tarun Plus (from 24 Oct 2024) covers ₹10-20 lakh for Tarun borrowers who repaid; Tarun is ₹5-10 lakh.

s: On which date was MUDRA Ltd, the refinancing agency under PMMY, set up?
x: MUDRA Ltd was set up on 18 March 2015, before PMMY was launched on 8 April 2015.

s: What was the maximum loan limit at the launch of PMMY in 2015?
x: The PMMY limit was ₹10 lakh at launch and is now ₹20 lakh with Tarun Plus.

s: What is the full form of MUDRA?
o: Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency
Micro Units Development and Regulatory Authority
Micro Undertakings Development and Rural Agency
Minor Units Deposit and Refinance Agency
x: MUDRA is the Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency, a SIDBI subsidiary that refinances lenders.

s: Up to what amount are loans given under the 'Shishu' category of PM MUDRA Yojana?
x: Shishu loans are up to ₹50,000; Kishore covers ₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (MUDRA category)
A. Shishu
B. Kishore
C. Tarun
D. Tarun Plus
List-II (Loan size)
1. ₹10-20 lakh
2. ₹5-10 lakh
3. ₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh
4. Up to ₹50,000
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Shishu is up to ₹50,000, Kishore ₹50,001-5 lakh, Tarun ₹5-10 lakh and Tarun Plus ₹10-20 lakh.

s:
Arrange the following in the order in which they were launched:
1. PM MUDRA Yojana
2. Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana
3. Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana
4. Digital Gender Atlas
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: PMJDY (28 Aug 2014), Digital Gender Atlas (9 Mar 2015), MUDRA (8 Apr 2015), PMSBY (9 May 2015).

s: What was the wider consequence of the microfinance crisis in Andhra Pradesh in 2010?
o: Converting all MFIs into payments banks
Ending the SHG-bank linkage programme across India
Prohibiting all forms of digital payments
Reshaping national regulation of microfinance institutions
x: The Andhra Pradesh microfinance crisis of 2010 contributed to changes that reshaped national regulation of MFIs.

s: On which date did the RBI create the NBFC-MFI category of NBFCs?
x: NBFC-MFI was created as a new RBI category on 2 December 2011; MFIN was formed in October 2009.

s: What is MFIN (Microfinance Institutions Network)?
o: Self-regulatory national body of RBI-regulated MFIs
x: MFIN, formed in October 2009, is a self-regulatory national body of RBI-regulated MFIs.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Microfinance Ordinance, 2010:
1. It was issued on 15 October 2010.
2. It required MFIs to register with a state-appointed authority.
3. It was never replaced by an Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The ordinance of 15 October 2010 required MFIs to register with a state-appointed authority; it was replaced by an Act in December 2010.

s: The SHG-bank linkage model was pioneered by which organisation during the mid-1980s?
x: MYRADA pioneered the SHG-bank linkage approach in the mid-1980s.

s: In which year was the NABARD pilot project for linking Self-Help Groups with banks launched?
x: NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage pilot in 1992. It became the world’s largest microfinance project, with banks lending to SHGs.

s: DAY-NRLM, launched in 2011 to promote rural livelihoods through SHGs, is run by which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: DAY-NRLM is a Ministry of Rural Development programme launched in 2011 for rural, not urban, livelihoods.

s: Andhra Pradesh, which ranks first in SHG-bank linkage, accounts for about what share of the national total?
x: AP ranks 1st with about 36% of the national share; its SHG model is run by SERP, not directly by NABARD.

s: When did DWCRA, an early women's group model in Andhra Pradesh, begin?
x: DWCRA (1982-83) was an early women's group model; NABARD's pilot came in 1992 and DAY-NRLM in 2011.

s: What is the recovery rate of SHG-bank loans in Andhra Pradesh?
x: AP ranks first in SHG-bank linkage with about 36% national share and 99.66% recovery.

s: The SHG-Bank Linkage pilot launched by NABARD in 1992 is regarded as the world's largest what?
x: NABARD's 1992 SHG-Bank Linkage pilot grew into the world's largest microfinance project.

s: Which body runs the SHG model in Andhra Pradesh?
x: In Andhra Pradesh the Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP) runs the SHG model, not NABARD directly.

s: The RBI Financial Inclusion Index was 53.9 in 2021. To what value did it rise in 2025?
x: The RBI FI-Index stood at 67.0 in 2025, up from 53.9 in 2021.

s: What incentive does the RuPay-BHIM UPI incentive scheme give on eligible BHIM-UPI person-to-merchant payments up to ₹2,000?
x: The scheme, run by DFS with NPCI as nodal agency, gives 0.15% on eligible P2M payments up to ₹2,000.

s: Under the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, UPI is to stay free for consumers. On which payments may MDR be imposed?
x: The Bill, passed by the Lok Sabha, lets the Centre modify zero-MDR so that MDR may apply to high-value payments while UPI stays free for consumers.

s: What is the base year of the Reserve Bank of India's Digital Payments Index (RBI-DPI)?
x: The RBI-DPI uses March 2018 as its base, with the index value fixed at 100. January 2021 marks the beginning of its publication, not its base year.

s: The RBI Financial Inclusion Index, introduced in 2021, comprises how many indicators?
x: The FI-Index has 97 indicators across banking, investment, insurance, postal and pension sectors, on a 0–100 scale, released annually in July.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the weights of the three sub-indices of the RBI Financial Inclusion Index?
x: The FI-Index assigns 35% to FI-Access, 45% to FI-Usage and 20% to FI-Quality.

s: Since when has zero MDR applied on RuPay debit card and BHIM-UPI transactions?
x: Zero MDR applies from 1 January 2020 under Section 10A of the PSS Act, 2007.

s: On whom does the zero-MDR model in India's digital payments mainly place a cost burden?
x: The cost of zero-MDR for payment system providers is a recognised concern, along with the digital divide and dormant Jan Dhan accounts.

s: How often is the RBI Digital Payments Index published?
x: RBI-DPI (base March 2018 = 100) is published semi-annually since January 2021.

s: How many parameters make up the RBI Digital Payments Index?
x: RBI-DPI has 5 parameters: payment enablers, payment infrastructure (demand and supply side), payment performance and consumer centricity.

s: On what scale is the RBI Financial Inclusion Index measured?
x: The FI-Index (since 2021, annual in July) is on a 0-100 scale; it stood at 67.0 in 2025.

s: Under the RuPay-BHIM UPI incentive scheme, which body acts as the nodal agency?
x: The scheme is run by DFS with NPCI as the nodal agency.

s: Who pays the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on a card payment?
o: The RBI, to the payment network
x: MDR is the fee a bank charges a merchant for accepting card payments; it is shared by the issuing bank, PoS bank and network.

s: What was the value of the RBI Financial Inclusion Index in 2025?
x: The RBI FI-Index, on a 0-100 scale, stood at 67.0 in 2025.

s: What was the value of the RBI Digital Payments Index for September 2025?
x: The RBI-DPI (base March 2018 = 100) reached 516.76 in September 2025.

s:
Consider the following about UPI:
1. It was launched in April 2016 with 21 banks.
2. It operates on the NEFT framework.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: UPI was launched in April 2016 with 21 banks and operates on the IMPS framework, not NEFT.

s: With which country is the UPI-PayNow linkage associated?
x: Singapore is associated with the UPI-PayNow linkage, which was established in 2023 after the initial 2021 connection.

s: Which country was the first country to adopt UPI services abroad through NPCI International Payments Limited?
x: Bhutan was the first country listed for UPI abroad, in 2021.

s: UPI accounted for approximately what share of the world's real-time payments in 2025?
x: UPI represented approximately 49% of the world's real-time payments in 2025.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched regarding international UPI linkages?
o: Bhutan — first country outside Asia to adopt UPI
Singapore — first country to adopt UPI for domestic cash withdrawals
France — first European country where UPI was enabled for e-commerce
x: France became the first European country where UPI was enabled for e-commerce. Singapore is associated with the UPI-PayNow remittance link, while Cambodia joined through NIPL and ACLEDA on the KHQR platform.

s: For what is the UPI feature 'UPI LITE X' meant?
x: UPI LITE X enables offline payments; Credit Line on UPI and Hello! UPI are other newer features.

s:
Consider the following about payments in India:
1. UPI has completely replaced cash for most of its users.
2. More than 90% of UPI users still use cash.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Over 90% of UPI users still use cash, so payment behaviour remains hybrid rather than fully digital.

s: For what is the UPI feature 'Hello! UPI' meant?
x: Hello! UPI enables voice payments; UPI LITE X is offline and UPI123Pay is for feature phones.

s: When did monthly UPI transactions first cross 2,000 crore?
x: UPI monthly transactions passed 2,000 crore for the first time in August 2025.

s: In FY 2025-26, UPI accounted for about what share of India's digital payment volume?
x: In FY 2025-26 UPI handled 24,160 crore transactions, about 85% of digital payment volume.

s: Through NPCI International Payments Ltd, UPI was live in how many countries in August 2026?
x: Through NIPL, UPI was live in 11 countries in August 2026, Bhutan (2021) being the first.

s: In which year was UPI launched in Qatar?
x: UPI went to Bhutan in 2021, the UAE in 2022, Nepal in 2024 and Qatar in 2025.

s: Through which bank's KHQR system was UPI launched in Cambodia in 2026?
x: NPCI International Payments Ltd linked UPI with ACLEDA Bank on the KHQR network in Cambodia (2026).

s: Promotion of digital payments was shifted from MeitY to which department of the Ministry of Finance?
x: Responsibility for promoting digital payments moved from MeitY to the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.

s: On which date did the wholesale pilot of India's e-rupee (e-rupee-W) begin?
x: The wholesale pilot began on 1 November 2022, and the retail pilot later, on 1 December 2022.

s: Through which law was the RBI Act amended to provide for the Digital Rupee?
x: The Finance Act, 2022 amended the RBI Act to cover digital currency; it did not make cryptocurrency legal tender.

s:
Consider the following:
1. UPI is money issued by the RBI.
2. The e-rupee is money itself and a liability of the RBI.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The e-rupee is an RBI liability; UPI is only a payment system that moves bank-account money.

s: The Bahamas' Sand Dollar is notable because it was
o: the world's first live retail CBDC, launched in 2020
the first wholesale CBDC pilot in the world
the first CBDC used exclusively for cross-border payments
the first cryptocurrency issued by a central bank
x: The Sand Dollar of the Bahamas was the world's first live retail CBDC and was launched in 2020.

s: What did the Supreme Court of India do in 2020 in a case relating to cryptocurrency?
o: Upheld the RBI's 2018 ban on banks dealing in cryptocurrency
Struck down the RBI's 2018 circular barring banks from dealing with cryptocurrency businesses
Declared cryptocurrency to be legal tender
Directed the RBI to launch the Digital Rupee
x: In 2020 the SC struck down the RBI's 2018 banking ban on crypto, so it was not upheld. Crypto is still not legal tender, and the 2021 bill to ban private crypto is pending. The Digital Rupee came through an amendment to the RBI Act (Finance Act 2022), not a court order, with pilots in Nov/Dec 2022.

s: At what rate are gains from cryptocurrency taxed in India?
x: Crypto gains attract 30% tax and 1% TDS; the 2021 bill to ban private crypto remains pending.

s: On which date did the retail pilot of India's e-rupee (e₹-R) begin?
x: The retail pilot (e₹-R) began on 1 December 2022; the wholesale pilot (e₹-W) on 1 November 2022.

s: In which year was Bitcoin, a peer-to-peer cryptocurrency not issued by any bank or government, created?
x: Bitcoin was created in January 2009 by Satoshi Nakamoto.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Act 2022:
1. It amended the RBI Act to provide for the Digital Rupee.
2. It made cryptocurrency legal tender in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Finance Act 2022 amended the RBI Act for the Digital Rupee; it did not make crypto legal tender but taxed gains at 30% with 1% TDS.

s: Who created Bitcoin?
x: Bitcoin was created in January 2009 by Satoshi Nakamoto as a peer-to-peer currency.

s: What was the name of the cryptocurrency announced by Facebook in 2019?
x: Facebook announced Libra in 2019; it was later renamed Diem.

s: What does an Account Aggregator primarily facilitate?
o: Compulsory transfer of all bank deposits to the RBI
Consent-based sharing of financial data among financial institutions
Direct lending by the Government to first-time borrowers
Issue of physical credit cards by payments banks
x: An Account Aggregator facilitates consent-based sharing of financial information, including bank transactions and GST records.

s: What share of their loans must small finance banks keep in loans of up to ₹25 lakh?
x: Small finance banks must have 50% of their loans up to ₹25 lakh; payments banks cannot lend at all.

s:
Assertion (A): Payments banks cannot issue credit cards.
Reason (R): Payments banks cannot lend directly to customers.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: a credit card is a lending product, and payments banks are not allowed to lend; they may accept deposits up to the initial ₹1 lakh limit, issue debit cards and hold G-secs.

s: What is OCEN?
o: A securities settlement system for stock exchanges
A deposit insurance scheme for payments banks
A common protocol linking lenders and marketplaces for small-ticket credit
A tax collection platform for State Governments
x: OCEN, or Open Credit Enablement Network, provides common protocols connecting lenders and marketplaces for small-ticket credit.

s: In the JAM trinity, what does the letter 'M' stand for?
x: JAM is Jan Dhan – Aadhaar – Mobile.

s: Which scheme forms the first layer of the JAM trinity that made Direct Benefit Transfer possible?
x: PMJDY (Jan Dhan) is the first layer of JAM and made paperless, presence-less DBT possible.

s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a part of the India Stack?
x: India Stack comprises Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, Account Aggregator and ONDC; RuPay is a domestic card network.

s: Up to what amount can payments banks now accept deposits?
x: Payments banks could take ₹1 lakh initially, raised to ₹2 lakh from 2021; they cannot lend.

s: The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is an initiative of which body?
x: ONDC, an open interoperable digital commerce network, is a DPIIT initiative.

s: Which body regulates Account Aggregators in India?
x: Account Aggregators are RBI-regulated NBFC-AAs that enable consent-based sharing of financial data.

s: What is the annual premium under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)?
x: PMSBY costs Rs 20 a year for ages 18-70, paying Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and Rs 1 lakh for partial disability.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Atal Pension Yojana?
o: It provides a pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 per month after age 60
Taxpayers cannot newly enrol from 1 October 2022
x: APY is administered under PFRDA, not IRDAI; the other statements are correct.

s: On which date were PMJJBY and PMSBY launched together?
x: PMJJBY and PMSBY, along with APY, were launched on 9 May 2015.

s: What is the annual premium of the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), as revised in 2022?
x: PMJJBY gives ₹2 lakh life cover for death from any cause at ₹436 a year (revised 2022, earlier ₹330); ₹20 is PMSBY.

s: Which body administers the Atal Pension Yojana?
x: APY is administered by PFRDA, not IRDAI.

s: What is the entry age for the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)?
x: PMJJBY covers ages 18-50; PMSBY covers 18-70 and APY 18-40.

s: What is the cover for partial permanent disability under PMSBY?
x: PMSBY pays ₹2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability.

s: What monthly pension from age 60 does the Atal Pension Yojana guarantee?
x: APY (ages 18-40) gives a pension of ₹1,000-5,000 a month from age 60.

s: What is the life cover under the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)?
x: PMJJBY gives ₹2 lakh life cover for death from any cause at ₹436 a year.

s: What is the entry age for the Atal Pension Yojana?
x: APY is open to people aged 18-40; PMJJBY is for 18-50 and PMSBY for 18-70.

s: What cover does PMSBY give for accidental death or full disability?
x: PMSBY gives ₹2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability, for ₹20 a year.

s: How is a G-Sec described under the Government Securities Act, 2006?
o: A tradeable instrument acknowledging debt of the Central or a State Government
A share issued by a government-owned company
An unsecured promissory note issued by a private company
A negotiable instrument issued only by commercial banks
x: A G-Sec is a tradeable instrument issued by the Central or State Government acknowledging government debt. It is issued by the RBI on behalf of the government under the Government Securities Act, 2006.

s: For what purpose are Cash Management Bills issued?
o: Temporary cash mismatches of the Central Government
Long-term borrowing needs of State Governments
Working-capital needs of public sector undertakings
x: CMBs cover the Centre's temporary cash mismatches; T-Bills are zero-coupon and SDLs are long-term State Government borrowings.

s: Treasury Bills differ from Government Bonds because Treasury Bills are:
x: Government Bonds pay interest, whereas Treasury Bills are zero-coupon securities.

s:
Consider the following about Government dated securities:
1. They have a maturity of at least one year.
2. They are issued only by State Governments.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Dated securities are long-term (one year or more) and issued by the Central Government; States issue State Development Loans.

s: What are dated securities issued by State Governments known as?
x: State Government dated securities are SDLs; Treasury Bills are short-term (91, 182, 364 days) Central instruments.

s: Which is the largest primary dealer in Government securities in India?
x: SBI DFHI is the largest primary dealer; primary dealers are RBI-regulated underwriters and market makers in G-Secs.

s: Through open market operations, what should the Reserve Bank of India generally do to absorb liquidity from the banking system?
x: An RBI sale of Government securities withdraws liquidity from the banking system. RBI purchases through OMOs inject liquidity.

s: Treasury Bills were first issued in India in which year?
x: India first issued Treasury Bills in 1917, during the First World War.

s: Through which account do individuals buy Government securities directly under RBI Retail Direct?
x: RBI Retail Direct lets individuals buy G-Secs directly through a Retail Direct Gilt account.

s: How much does Andhra Pradesh plan to borrow through State Development Loans in 2026-27?
x: AP plans SDL borrowings of ₹73,383 crore in 2026-27; ₹55,518 crore was the record FPI bond inflow of June 2026.

s: What is the market for Treasury Bills and Government bonds known as?
x: The gilt-edged market is the market of government securities such as T-bills and Government bonds.

s: Why are government securities called 'gilt-edged'?
o: Their default risk is almost zero
They are sold only to foreign investors
They pay the highest interest in the market
x: Interest and repayment on government securities are sure on the due date, so their default risk is almost zero.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The gilt-edged market deals in government securities.
2. Debentures of private companies are traded in the gilt-edged market.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The gilt-edged market covers T-bills and Government bonds, not corporate paper.

s: Which of the following is NOT a maturity at which Government of India Treasury Bills are issued?
x: T-bills are issued for 91, 182 and 364 days; securities of one year or more are dated G-Secs.

s: What is the longest maturity of a Treasury Bill issued by the Government of India?
x: T-bills are short-term, with maturities of 91, 182 and 364 days.

s: Who issues Treasury Bills in India, and how are they sold?
o: The Central Government, through RBI auctions
x: T-bills are issued by the Centre and sold by the RBI through auctions; State dated securities are SDLs.

s: Under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR), which of the following were newly covered in June 2026?
x: In June 2026 FAR was extended to new 15-, 30- and 40-year G-Secs and sovereign green bonds.

s: Which body regulates the money market (instruments of up to one year maturity) in India?
x: The money market is regulated by the RBI and the capital market (maturity above one year) by SEBI.

s: Which of the following is a capital-market instrument?
x: Equity shares are a pure capital-market instrument; T-bills, CPs and CDs are money-market instruments.

s: Which of the following is a sub-market of the money market rather than the capital market?
x: The Call Money and Treasury Bill markets belong to the money market; the Government Bond and Stock markets to the capital market.

s: Which of the following is correctly classified as a hybrid capital-market instrument?
x: Convertible preference shares and partly or optionally convertible debentures are hybrid instruments. Equity shares are pure instruments, while T-Bills and CPs belong to the money market.

s: On what did the Budget 2026–27 framework for financial markets propose derivatives?
x: The framework included market-making for corporate bonds, derivatives on corporate bond indices and support for bigger municipal bond markets.

s: Into which segments is the industrial securities market, a part of the Indian capital market, divided?
x: The industrial securities market has primary and secondary segments; DFIs and intermediaries such as venture capital companies are other parts of the capital market.

s: Which one of the following correctly matches the regulator with the central counterparties (CCPs) it regulates?
o: RBI — CCIL for money, G-Sec and forex markets; SEBI — NSCCL and ICCL for capital markets
SEBI — CCIL; RBI — NSCCL and ICCL
RBI — all CCPs including NSCCL and ICCL
x: The RBI regulates CCPs in the money, G-Sec and forex markets (CCIL), and SEBI regulates capital-market CCPs (NSCCL, ICCL). Option B reverses them, option C wrongly gives every CCP to the RBI, and IFSCA regulates only IFSC entities.

s: Exchange-traded funds such as the CPSE ETF and Bharat-22 ETF trade on exchanges at prices close to what?
x: ETFs trade on exchanges close to their net asset value (NAV).

s: What is investment in unlisted firms known as?
x: Private equity is investment in unlisted firms; venture capital is a form of private equity.

s: India's corporate bond market is about what share of GDP?
x: Corporate bonds are about 16% of GDP in India against 79% in Korea; about 98% are privately placed.

s: Which form of finance provides long-term start-up capital to new firms with growth potential?
x: Venture capital is long-term start-up capital for new firms; promoting it is part of entrepreneur development.

s: Venture capital is a form of which type of investment?
x: Venture capital is a form of private equity that funds new firms and supports entrepreneur development.

s: Hedge funds that use leveraged trading fall under which SEBI category of Alternative Investment Funds?
x: Hedge funds and leveraged trading are Category III (which may also trade commodity derivatives); Category II is private equity and debt funds.

s: In September 2025, SEBI added an Alternative Investment Fund category specifically for which group?
x: In September 2025, SEBI added an AIF category intended only for accredited investors.

s:
Consider the following:
1. REITs pool real-estate assets.
2. InvITs pool real-estate assets.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: REITs pool real-estate assets, while InvITs pool infrastructure assets.

s: Venture capital and angel funds fall under which SEBI category of Alternative Investment Funds?
x: Category I covers venture capital, angel, SME, social venture and infrastructure funds; hedge funds are Category III.

s: Private equity and debt funds fall under which SEBI AIF category?
x: Category II covers private equity and debt funds such as the Self-Reliant India Fund.

s: In which year's SEBI (AIF) Regulations are Alternative Investment Funds defined?
x: AIFs are privately pooled funds defined under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012.

s: Which of the following is part of the unorganised money market?
x: Indigenous bankers, moneylenders, chit funds and hundis form the unorganised market; money market mutual funds and DFHI are organised.

s: Which of the following is NOT part of the organised money market?
x: Moneylenders belong to the unorganised money market, which is not controlled by the RBI.

s: Which institutions are placed between the organised and unorganised money markets?
x: Co-operative credit institutions sit between the two segments.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian money market:
1. The unorganised money market is not controlled by the RBI.
2. Call money is the most unstable part of the organised money market.
3. Hundis are part of the organised money market.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The unorganised segment is outside RBI control and call money (repayable on demand) is the most unstable part; hundis are unorganised.

s: What is an unsecured short-term promissory instrument issued by eligible corporates called?
x: Commercial Paper is an unsecured short-term promissory instrument issued by eligible corporates.

s: On the recommendation of which committee was Commercial Paper introduced in India in 1990?
x: CP (1990) and CDs (1989) both came on the Vaghul Committee's recommendation; CP can now be issued for 7 days to 1 year.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Commercial Paper is an unsecured promissory note; call money is overnight, notice money runs 2 to 14 days and TREPS is a tri-party repo.

s: In which year was the Certificate of Deposit introduced in India?
x: On the Vaghul Committee's advice, CDs began in 1989 and Commercial Paper in 1990.

s: What is the maturity of Certificates of Deposit issued by financial institutions?
x: Bank CDs run up to 1 year; CDs of FIs run 1 to 3 years.

s: For what maturity can Commercial Paper be issued?
x: CP is issued for 7 days to 1 year by eligible corporates.

s: Which body operated CBLO, introduced in January 2003?
x: CBLO was introduced by the CCIL from 20 January 2003; it was later replaced by TREPS.

s: What is the usual maturity of commercial bills drawn by firms and discounted by banks?
x: Commercial bills are trade bills, usually of about 90 days, discounted by banks.

s: Which money market arrangement replaced CBLO?
x: TREPS, a tri-party repo in which a third party handles collateral and settlement, replaced CBLO.

s: Which of the following generally tends to LOWER government bond yields?
o: RBI purchases of G-secs through OMOs
x: OMO purchases support bond prices and inject liquidity, lowering yields; higher policy rates, inflation and borrowing raise yields.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Treasury Bills – issued at a discount and redeemed at face value
Face value – nominal value printed on a security
Dated government bonds – pay periodic coupon interest
Yield – nominal value printed on a security
x: Yield is the investor's return at the market price; the nominal value printed on a security is its face value.

s: What is the date on which a bond's principal becomes repayable called?
x: The repayment date is maturity; the coupon is the interest, and face value is the nominal value.

s: In relation to the issuer, what is a bondholder?
x: A bondholder lends to the issuer and is therefore its creditor.

s: Who bears the currency risk in a Masala bond?
x: A Masala bond is rupee-denominated and issued overseas, so the investor bears the currency risk.

s: What rate of interest did the Sovereign Gold Bond scheme, launched in 2015, pay in addition to gold-price-linked returns?
x: SGBs were launched in 2015 with 2.5% interest plus gold-price-linked returns; fresh issuance has been discontinued.

s: Which institution issued the first green bond in 2007?
x: The European Investment Bank issued the first green bond in 2007; the World Bank issued a labelled green bond in 2008.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about bonds?
o: Market yield and bond price generally move in opposite directions
Yield is the return earned by an investor
Maturity is the date on which the principal is repaid
Coupon is the nominal value of the bond
x: The coupon is the interest payment; the nominal value is the face value. Price and yield move inversely and yield is the investor's return.

s: What is a bond whose proceeds finance only social projects called?
x: A social bond funds only social projects; a sustainability bond funds both environmental and social projects.

s: What is a rupee-denominated bond issued overseas called?
x: A Masala bond is rupee-denominated and issued abroad, so the investor bears the currency risk.

s: Which of the following tends to RAISE government bond yields?
x: Higher policy rates, inflation and government borrowing raise yields; RBI OMO purchases and foreign inflows lower them.

s:
Consider the following statements about bonds:
1. A zero-coupon bond is issued at a discount and pays no periodic interest.
2. New issues of Sovereign Gold Bonds have been stopped.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Zero-coupon bonds such as T-bills are issued at a discount without periodic interest, and new SGB issues have been stopped.

s: An inflation-indexed bond is one whose:
o: Interest is linked to the gold price
Currency risk is borne by the investor
Principal or coupon is adjusted to inflation
x: Inflation-indexed bonds adjust principal or coupon to inflation; climate-only funding is a green bond.

s:
Consider the following:
1. Jim O'Neill coined the term BRIC in 2001.
2. The first BRIC Summit was held in 2008.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: O'Neill coined 'BRIC' in 2001; the first BRIC summit was held in 2009 at Yekaterinburg, not 2008.

s: What are the base year and base value of the SENSEX respectively?
x: The SENSEX has 1978–79 as its base year and a base value of 100.

s: Which one of the following is NOT a share-price index?
x: Moody’s is a ratings agency, not a share-price index. SENSEX, NIFTY 50 and DOLLEX-30 are market indices.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the SENSEX?
o: A dollar-linked index of 30 NSE stocks
A BSE index of 20 carbon-efficient companies
An NSE index of 50 stocks from 13 sectors calculated on the basis of full market capitalisation
A BSE index of 30 blue-chip stocks calculated on the basis of free-float market capitalisation
x: SENSEX comprises 30 blue-chip stocks listed on the BSE and is calculated using the free-float market capitalisation method.

s: In which year was the NIFTY 50 index launched?
x: NIFTY 50 was launched in 1996; it has 50 stocks from 13 sectors and uses free-float market capitalisation.

s: On what basis does BSE GREENEX select companies?
x: GREENEX tracks top green companies chosen by GHG emissions, i.e. carbon efficiency; the dollar-linked index is DOLLEX-30.

s: DOLLEX-30, a dollar-linked version of the Sensex launched in 2001, is an index of which exchange?
x: DOLLEX-30 is a BSE index of 30 stocks, launched on 25 July 2001 as a dollar-linked Sensex.

s: By which method is the NIFTY 50 index calculated?
x: Both the Sensex and the NIFTY 50 are free-float market-capitalisation weighted indices.

s: What are the base date and base value of the NIFTY 50?
x: NIFTY 50 has base 3 Nov 1995 = 1000 and was launched on 22 April 1996; 1978-79 = 100 is the Sensex base.

s: In which year was the SENSEX first published?
x: The SENSEX was first published on 1 January 1986, with base 1978-79 = 100.

s: In which year was BSE GREENEX launched?
x: BSE GREENEX, an index of carbon-efficient companies, was launched on 22 February 2012.

s: Which body manages the NIFTY 50 index?
x: NIFTY 50 is managed by NSE Indices Ltd (formerly IISL), a subsidiary of NSE.

s: Which country overtook India, pushing it to 7th place in global stock market capitalisation?
x: India fell to 7th in global market capitalisation after being overtaken by South Korea.

s:
Consider the following about the BSE:
1. It was established in 1992 by financial institutions.
2. It was first recognised under the SCRA on 31 August 1957.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: BSE was recognised under the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act on 31 August 1957; it was formally set up in 1875.

s: Which body regulates exchanges located in the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) at GIFT City?
x: IFSC exchanges such as India INX (30 Dec 2016, India's first international exchange) and NSEIX are regulated by IFSCA, not SEBI.

s: Which is Asia's oldest stock exchange, set up in 1875 on Dalal Street?
x: BSE (1875) is Asia's oldest exchange; NSE was India's first fully automated electronic exchange.

s: Which of the following was among the original promoters of NSE?
x: IDBI was among the NSE's original promoters, with SBI, IFCI, LIC, GIC and IDFC. The Pherwani Committee recommended the NSE, and SEBI regulates it.

s: Which was the first segment launched by the National Stock Exchange?
x: NSE (set up November 1992, recognised April 1993, trading from 1994) launched the Wholesale Debt Market first, not the Cash Market.

s: In which year did BSE move to Dalal Street?
x: Brokers moved to Dalal Street in 1874, and the BSE was formally set up in 1875.

s: Which body promoted the depository CDSL?
x: CDSL was promoted by BSE, while NSDL was India's first depository.

s: On the recommendation of which committee was the NSE set up in November 1992?
x: NSE was set up on the Pherwani Committee's recommendation; the Gupta and Varma committees designed the F&O market.

s: Which is India's first international exchange, set up at GIFT City IFSC on 30 December 2016?
x: India INX, a BSE subsidiary at GIFT City IFSC, is India's first international exchange (2016).

s: Under which name did the Metropolitan Stock Exchange (MSE) begin in 2008?
x: MSE began in 2008 as MCX-SX and was renamed in 2015.

s:
Consider the following statements about Indian stock exchanges:
1. BSE is Asia's oldest stock exchange.
2. NSE was India's first fully automated electronic exchange.
3. India INX at GIFT City is regulated by SEBI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: BSE (1875) is Asia's oldest and NSE was the first fully automated exchange; IFSC exchanges like India INX are regulated by IFSCA, not SEBI.

s: Which stock exchange handles the largest volume of stock market business in India?
x: The NSE had the highest turnover from 2000-01 and is still the largest exchange in India by volume.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The NSE is India's largest stock exchange by trading volume.
2. The BSE is Asia's oldest stock exchange.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The NSE leads in volume, and the BSE, set up in 1875, is Asia's oldest exchange.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about depositories in India?
o: Depositories hold shares in demat form
NSDL was set up in Mumbai in 1996
x: CDSL was promoted by BSE, not NSE; NSDL (Mumbai, 6 Nov 1996) was the first depository.

s: Which was India's first depository?
x: NSDL was India's first depository; BSE is Asia's oldest exchange and India INX India's first international exchange.

s: When was NSE, set up in November 1992, recognised by SEBI?
x: NSE was set up in November 1992 and recognised in April 1993; 1988 and April 1992 are SEBI's non-statutory and statutory milestones.

s: What is a circuit breaker in a securities market intended to do?
o: Halt trading when an index or stock moves beyond prescribed limits
x: A circuit breaker temporarily halts trading when the movement in an index or stock exceeds specified limits.

s: When does settlement take place under the standard T+1 settlement cycle?
o: Five trading days after the transaction
One trading day after the transaction
On the same calendar day only
x: T+1 denotes settlement one trading day after the transaction. Optional same-day T+0 settlement is also available.

s: What is an investor who buys IPO shares to sell them quickly on listing called?
x: A stag buys IPO shares to sell soon after listing; a bear expects prices to fall and a bull expects a rise.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Blue Chip – shares of large, well-established and financially sound companies
Beta – shares of large, well-established and financially sound companies
CDSL – depository initially promoted by BSE
x: Beta measures fluctuation or systematic risk relative to the market; shares of large, sound companies are blue chips.

s: In the stock market, what does the beta of a security measure?
o: Systematic risk compared with the market
x: Beta measures a security's systematic risk relative to the market; a beta of 1 means it moves with the market.

s: What are shares given to employees or directors for know-how or services, often at a discount, called?
x: Sweat equity is issued to employees or directors for know-how or services, often at a discount.

s: What is selling borrowed shares in the hope of buying them back at a lower price called?
x: Short selling means selling borrowed shares and buying them back lower.

s: In the stock market, who is a 'bull'?
o: An investor who expects prices to rise
An investor who expects prices to fall
An investor who buys IPO shares to sell on listing
A broker who trades for clients
x: A bull expects prices to rise; a bear expects them to fall and a stag buys IPO shares to sell on listing.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Term)
A. Bull
B. Bear
C. Stag
List-II (Meaning)
1. Buys IPO shares to sell on listing
2. Expects prices to fall
3. Expects prices to rise
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Bull expects a rise, bear expects a fall and stag buys IPO shares to sell soon after listing.

s: At least what share of their investments does SEBI require arbitrage mutual funds to keep in equity?
x: Arbitrage funds must keep at least 65% (not 75%) in equity; mutual fund units are priced at NAV.

s: Who holds the residual claim on a company's earnings and assets?
x: Shareholders are owners with a residual claim; debenture and bondholders are creditors paid before them.

s: In 2016, SEBI called online platforms offering which activity unauthorised?
x: Equity crowdfunding is not permitted in India; SEBI called online platforms offering it unauthorised in 2016.

s: At what are units of a mutual fund priced?
x: A mutual fund pools money and its units are priced at NAV.

s: Which derivative contract gives its holder a right but not an obligation?
x: An option gives a right but not an obligation; a futures contract creates an obligation to buy or sell at a fixed future price.

s: What rights do a call option and a put option respectively provide?
o: Exchange fixed and floating interest only
x: A call option gives the right to buy, while a put option gives the right to sell.

s: Into which body was the Forward Markets Commission merged in 2015?
x: The FMC was merged into SEBI, not the RBI, in 2015.

s: Which committees are associated with the development of India's futures and options market?
o: L.C. Gupta and J.R. Varma Committees
x: The L.C. Gupta Committee (1998) and the J.R. Varma Committee (2002) shaped India's F&O market.

s: To what did the Budget 2026–27 raise the Securities Transaction Tax on futures from 0.02%?
x: STT on futures rose from 0.02% to 0.05% and on options from 0.10% to 0.15%.

s: What was the main aim of the increase in Securities Transaction Tax (STT) on futures and options (F&O) in the Budget 2026–27?
o: Curb speculation in the derivatives market
Provide interest subsidies to IPO applicants
Replace the Goods and Services Tax on equity trades
x: The STT hike on F&O in Budget 2026–27 was aimed at curbing speculation. It was not intended to subsidise IPO applications or replace GST.

s: According to SEBI, how many out of ten option traders in India lost money?
x: SEBI found that nine out of ten option traders lost money; India's options market is among the world's largest by contracts.

s: What does a futures contract give its holder?
o: An obligation to buy or sell at a fixed future price
A right but not an obligation to buy
A right but not an obligation to sell
An exchange of fixed and floating interest flows
x: Futures carry an obligation; options give a right without obligation, and swaps exchange cash flows.

s: Which exchange launched India's first weather derivative, RAINMUMBAI?
x: NCDEX's RAINMUMBAI is India's first weather derivative.

s: In Q1 2024, Indian exchanges handled about what share of equity options traded worldwide?
x: Indian exchanges handled about 84% of equity options traded worldwide in Q1 2024.

s: What is a derivative in which two parties exchange cash flows, such as fixed against floating interest, called?
x: A swap is an exchange of cash flows, such as fixed versus floating interest.

s: At what rate was the Commodity Transaction Tax, introduced in Budget 2013-14, levied?
x: CTT came in Budget 2013-14 at 0.01%; 0.02% and 0.05% are the old and new STT rates on futures.

s: To what did the Budget 2026-27 raise the Securities Transaction Tax on options from 0.10%?
x: Budget 2026-27 raised STT on options from 0.10% to 0.15% (futures 0.02% to 0.05%) to curb speculation.

s: In what does the secondary market deal?
x: The secondary market trades securities already issued; SEBI regulates stock exchange operations.

s: Between whom do transactions in the primary market take place?
o: Investors among themselves on a stock exchange
x: In the primary market a company sells new securities to investors; trading between investors happens in the secondary market.

s: In an IPO, to whom do the proceeds of an offer for sale go?
x: In an offer for sale existing owners sell their holdings and receive the proceeds; only a fresh issue brings money to the firm.

s: In which market does trading in existing gilt-edged securities take place?
x: Gilt-edged trading of existing securities is a secondary-market activity; the primary (new issue) market deals in new securities.

s: Which of the following is NOT a primary-market transaction?
x: IPOs, FPOs and rights issues are primary-market issues; stock-exchange trading of existing shares is secondary-market activity.

s: In the book-building process of an IPO, investors bid within a:
o: Single price fixed before any bids
Price band, and the final price is set from the bids
Price set by the stock exchange after listing
Price equal to the face value
x: In book building, bids are made within a price band from floor to cap, and the final price is determined from the bids received.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IPO process?
o: A Greenshoe option lets the issuer sell extra shares when demand is high
Anchor investors are retail investors who bid after the issue closes
Anchor investors are QIBs who bid before the issue opens
Under ASBA, application money stays blocked in the investor's account until allotment
x: Anchor investors are QIBs who bid before the issue opens, with a lock-in; they are not retail investors bidding after closure.

s: An SME IPO is required to be listed within which period from the closing of the issue?
x: Listing must take place within T+3 days of the issue closing (T = issue-closing day); SME IPOs list on separate platforms such as BSE SME and NSE Emerge under the same timeline.

s: For very large companies, to what may the minimum portion offered to the public in an IPO be reduced?
x: The public offer portion for very large companies may be 2.75%. This represented a reduction from the earlier requirement of 5%.

s: Who are anchor investors in an Indian IPO?
o: QIBs who bid before the issue opens, with a lock-in
Retail investors who bid after listing
Promoters selling through an offer for sale
Stags who sell soon after listing
x: Anchor investors are Qualified Institutional Buyers bidding before the issue opens, and their shares carry a lock-in.

s: On which separate platforms are SME IPOs in India listed?
o: Wholesale Debt Market and Cash Market
x: SME IPOs list on BSE SME and NSE Emerge; India INX and NSE IX are GIFT City exchanges and NSDL/CDSL are depositories.

s: What is the full form of ASBA in IPO applications?
x: ASBA is Application Supported by Blocked Amount: the application money is blocked in the investor's account and debited only on allotment.

s: In which year did SEBI introduce ASBA for public issues?
x: SEBI introduced Application Supported by Blocked Amount (ASBA) in 2008.

s: What does the primary market deal in?
x: The primary market deals in new securities and the secondary market in existing ones.

s: What does the secondary market deal in?
x: The secondary market is for trading existing securities; new issues come in the primary market.

s: Which body regulates and monitors mutual funds in India?
x: SEBI regulates and monitors mutual funds and also works to prevent scams in the capital market.

s: Which of the following comes under the RBI rather than SEBI?
x: Credit rating agencies, mutual funds and depositories like CDSL are regulated by SEBI; government securities come under the RBI.

s: Which body regulates the pension sector in India?
x: PFRDA regulates pensions; SEBI the capital market, the RBI money and banking, and NABARD agricultural credit.

s: Which body regulates agricultural credit in India?
x: NABARD covers agricultural credit; SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA cover capital markets, insurance and pensions.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: SEBI regulates the capital market; insurance is IRDAI's, pensions PFRDA's, and money and banking the RBI's.

s: Which of the following entities is included among Market Infrastructure Institutions regulated by SEBI?
o: Commercial banks acting as monetary authorities
x: Stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories are identified as Market Infrastructure Institutions regulated by SEBI.

s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of entities regulated by SEBI?
o: Money-market CCPs, G-Sec CCPs and forex CCPs
Currency-issuing offices, RBI and monetary-policy committees
State treasuries, commercial-tax offices and customs houses
x: Mutual funds, Alternative Investment Funds and Foreign Portfolio Investors are regulated by SEBI. Money-market, government-security and foreign-exchange CCPs remain with the RBI.

s: Which body regulates clearing corporations (CCPs) for the money, G-Sec and forex markets?
x: Money-market, G-Sec and forex CCPs remain with the RBI, while capital-market CCPs fall under SEBI.

s: Which body regulates credit rating agencies in India?
x: Credit rating agencies are regulated by SEBI, not by the RBI.

s: In which year was UTI established?
x: UTI, India's first mutual fund, was set up in 1964. Public-sector mutual funds other than UTI came in 1987, and private ones in 1993.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Non-UTI public-sector mutual funds set up – 1993
Non-UTI public-sector mutual funds set up – 1996
x: SEBI's first Mutual Funds Regulations came in 1993; non-UTI public-sector funds came in 1987 and the revised regulations in 1996.

s: Which was India's first credit rating agency, set up in 1987?
x: CRISIL (1987) came first, followed by ICRA (1991) and CARE (1993).

s: Foreign Portfolio Investors register with SEBI through which single-window system launched in 2025?
x: FPIs come through the SWAFAT-FI single window (2025); SCORES is the complaints system.

s: Which body regulates REITs and InvITs in India?
x: REITs and InvITs are among the entities regulated by SEBI.

s: Under which Act was UTI, India's first mutual fund, set up?
x: UTI was set up on 1 February 1964 under the UTI Act, 1963.

s: In which year did the SEBI Stock Brokers Regulations replace the 1992 rules for stock brokers?
x: The Stock Brokers Regulations 2026 replaced the 1992 rules in January 2026.

s: How many REITs were listed in India in 2026?
x: India had 5 listed REITs in 2026, with AUM above ₹2.25 lakh crore.

s: From which body did SEBI take over on getting statutory powers in 1992?
x: SEBI (set up 12 April 1988, statutory from 30 January 1992) took over from the Controller of Capital Issues; the FMC merged into SEBI only in 2015.

s: Which of the following is NOT an objective stated in the Preamble of the SEBI Act, 1992?
o: Regulating the lending rates of commercial banks
Protecting the interests of investors in securities
Promoting the development of the securities market
x: Bank lending rates come under the RBI; the Preamble covers investor protection and the development and regulation of the securities market.

s: Who took charge as Chairperson of SEBI in 2025?
x: Tuhin Kanta Pandey took charge as SEBI Chairperson in 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the composition of the SEBI Board?
o: Five other members are included, at least three of them whole-time
Two members are drawn from the Finance and Law ministries
Two members are drawn from the Reserve Bank of India
x: The SEBI Board has one member from the RBI, not two; the other statements describe its composition correctly.

s:
Consider the following statements about SEBI:
1. Its parent law is the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.
2. It began in 1988 as a non-statutory body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: SEBI began in 1988 as a non-statutory body; its parent law is the SEBI Act, 1992, not the SCRA.

s: SEBI functions under which Ministry of the Government of India?
x: SEBI, headquartered in Mumbai, is under the Ministry of Finance; the IEPF Authority is under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

s: Where is the headquarters of SEBI located?
x: SEBI is headquartered in Mumbai.

s: What is the parent law of SEBI?
x: SEBI's parent law is the SEBI Act, 1992, not the SCRA, 1956.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Securities Appellate Tribunal set up
2. NSE recognised
3. SEBI gets statutory status
4. Forward Markets Commission merged into SEBI
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: SEBI became statutory in 1992, NSE was recognised in April 1993, SAT came in 1995 and FMC merged into SEBI in 2015.

s: The Securities Markets Code Bill, 2025, introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2025, proposes to merge which set of laws?
o: RBI Act, 1934; Banking Regulation Act, 1949; FEMA, 1999
Companies Act, 2013; GST Act, 2017; Income-tax Act, 1961
x: The Bill proposes to merge the SEBI Act, 1992, the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 and the Depositories Act, 1996.

s: Which body prescribes the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) for the top 1,000 listed companies?
x: BRSR is prescribed by SEBI (not the RBI) and replaced the earlier BRR; BRSR Core needs reasonable assurance on key ESG metrics.

s: Which of the following is true of T+0 settlement in Indian stock markets?
x: T+0 is an optional same-day settlement alongside T+1, aimed at liquidity and lower settlement and counterparty risk.

s: With which company did SEBI introduce a verified 'tick mark' for broker apps?
x: SEBI and Google introduced the verified tick mark for broker apps; stock tips by finfluencers need SEBI registration.

s: What must a finfluencer giving stock tips or return claims do under SEBI rules?
x: Stock tips or return claims are advisory work needing SEBI registration.

s:
Consider the following statements about the BRSR:
1. It replaced the Business Responsibility Report (BRR).
2. BRSR Core needs reasonable assurance on key ESG metrics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: BRSR replaced the BRR, and BRSR Core needs reasonable assurance on key ESG metrics.

s: Under the Securities Markets Code Bill, 2025, how many members may the SEBI board have at most?
x: The Bill allows a SEBI board of up to 15 members and gives MIIs statutory status.

s: In which city did AP MSME Development Corporation and NSE run an SME IPO awareness programme?
x: The SME IPO awareness programme by AP MSME Development Corporation and NSE was held in Vijayawada.

s: What are the main aims of the optional T+0 (same-day) settlement introduced by SEBI?
o: Higher brokerage income for stock exchanges
Better liquidity and lower settlement and counterparty risk
x: T+0 is optional and runs alongside T+1; it aims at better liquidity, lower settlement and counterparty risk and more efficiency.

s: By how much did SME IPOs in India surge during FY23-FY25?
x: SME IPOs surged 87% over FY23-25; SEBI's chief still called the SME market under-scaled.

s: Which entities get statutory status under the Securities Markets Code Bill, 2025?
x: The Bill gives statutory status to MIIs such as stock exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Forward Markets Commission (FMC):
1. It merged with SEBI in 2014.
2. Set up in 1953, it regulated commodity futures markets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The FMC (1953) regulated commodity futures and merged with SEBI in 2015, not 2014.

s: The Forward Markets Commission worked under which law?
x: FMC, set up in 1953, worked under the Forward Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1952.

s: After the FMC merger with SEBI, which category of AIFs was allowed into commodity derivatives?
x: After the 2015 merger, Category III AIFs were allowed in commodity derivatives.

s: The Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) Authority functions under which of the following?
o: SEBI Act, 1992 and Ministry of Finance
Companies Act, 2013 and Ministry of Corporate Affairs
Forward Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1952 and Ministry of Commerce
Companies Act, 1956 and Ministry of Corporate Affairs
x: The IEPF Authority was established under the Companies Act, 2013 and functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

s: The Securities Appellate Tribunal was set up in which year under the SEBI Act?
x: The Securities Appellate Tribunal was set up in 1995 under the SEBI Act.

s: Inspection, search and seizure come under which type of SEBI's powers?
x: Inspection, search and seizure are investigative; framing regulations is quasi-legislative; orders, penalties and disgorgement are quasi-judicial.

s: Where does an appeal against an order of the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) lie?
x: SAT hears appeals against SEBI and stock exchanges; a further appeal lies to the Supreme Court, not the RBI.

s: SEBI's power to pass disgorgement orders is part of which type of its powers?
x: Orders, penalties and disgorgement are quasi-judicial powers; framing regulations is quasi-legislative.

s: Which body hears appeals against the orders of SEBI and stock exchanges?
x: The Securities Appellate Tribunal (1995, SEBI Act Section 15K) hears appeals against SEBI and stock exchanges; further appeal lies to the Supreme Court.

s: Under which Section of the SEBI Act was the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) set up?
x: SAT was set up in 1995 under Section 15K of the SEBI Act.

s: Who heads the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT)?
o: Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court
x: SAT has a Presiding Officer and members; it is separate from SEBI, whose orders it hears in appeal.

s: For what total amount did NSE settle the co-location and dark fibre cases, after which the Supreme Court disposed of SEBI's appeals?
x: NSE paid ₹1,492 crore (₹1,224 crore + ₹268 crore) in the settlement.

s: What do SEBI's PFUTP Regulations prohibit to protect investors?
x: PFUTP stands for Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices, which is why the regulations protect investors.

s: What is SCORES, associated with investor protection in the securities market?
o: An online complaints redress system of SEBI
A commodity futures exchange operated by NSE
A statutory fund for refunding unclaimed dividends
x: SCORES is SEBI’s online system for redressal of investor complaints.

s: Insider trading means trading on which kind of information?
x: Insider trading is trading on non-public, material information.

s: On which Foundation Day of SEBI was 'Mission Jagrook' launched?
x: SEBI launched Mission Jagrook on its 38th Foundation Day.

s: The 2025 amendment to SEBI's Prohibition of Insider Trading (PIT) Regulations widened the meaning of which of the following?
x: The 2025 PIT amendment widened the definition of UPSI.

s: The RBI Retail Direct Scheme lets retail investors buy which securities directly from the RBI?
x: Retail Direct lets retail investors buy G-Secs directly from the RBI; G-Secs stay with the RBI, not SEBI.

s: In which year did SEBI issue its REIT and InvIT Regulations?
x: SEBI's REIT and InvIT Regulations (2014) let real-estate and infrastructure assets raise money from investors.

s: Under SEBI's large corporate borrowing framework, what must large listed companies do?
o: Raise a part of fresh borrowing through bonds
x: Large listed companies must raise a part of their fresh borrowing through bonds.

s: Why did SEBI lower the ticket (face value) size of corporate bonds?
o: To keep retail investors out of the bond market
To raise the cost of bond issues
To shift corporate bonds to RBI regulation
To draw retail investors into the bond market
x: A smaller face value lets small (retail) investors buy corporate bonds.

s: Who frames the regulations for the issue and listing of municipal bonds in India?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: Municipal debt securities are issued and listed under SEBI regulations.

s: The Ketan Parekh scam of 2001 is associated with which market reform?
o: Ending badla and introducing rolling settlement
x: The Ketan Parekh scam was associated with the ending of badla and the move to rolling settlement.

s: To which reform did Satyam's 2009 accounting fraud, popularly called India's Enron, contribute?
o: Audit and board reforms under the Companies Act, 2013 and creation of NFRA
The merger of FMC with SEBI
x: The Satyam scandal led to audit and board reforms in the Companies Act, 2013 and the establishment of the National Financial Reporting Authority.

s: After the Sahara OFCD case, at how many investors was private placement of securities capped?
x: The Sahara case led to a cap of 50 investors for private placement and SEBI power over deemed public issues.

s: The Harshad Mehta scam of 1992 pushed which reform?
o: End of badla and rolling settlement
Statutory powers for SEBI and screen-based trading on NSE
x: Harshad Mehta pushed SEBI's statutory powers and NSE's screen trading; badla ended after Ketan Parekh.

s: What did the Sodhi Committee of SEBI deal with?
o: Separation of Chairman and MD/CEO posts
x: The Sodhi Committee framed principle-based insider-trading regulations; Clause 49 came from the K. M. Birla Committee.

s: What did the T. K. Viswanathan Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee (2015) form the basis of?
x: The Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee's work formed the basis of the IBC, 2016; it was not a SEBI committee.

s: Which committee gave Clause 49 of the listing agreement on corporate governance?
x: The K. M. Birla Committee (1999) gave Clause 49 on corporate governance.

s: Which SEBI committee (2017) recommended separating the posts of Chairman and MD/CEO?
x: The Uday Kotak Committee (2017) recommended at least half the board independent and separate Chairman and MD/CEO.

s: What did the T. K. Viswanathan Committee appointed by SEBI in 2017 deal with?
x: The 2017 SEBI committee dealt with fair market conduct; the 2015 T. K. Viswanathan committee was on bankruptcy law.

s: In which of the following did the Global Financial Crisis of 2007-09 originate?
x: The GFC began with US sub-prime mortgages; India then saw FPI outflows and set up the FSDC in December 2010.

s: Teaser loans are loans with which feature?
o: No repayment obligation during the entire loan period
A high fixed interest rate initially and a lower rate later
A low fixed interest rate in the early years and a higher rate subsequently
Only a floating interest rate linked to gold prices
x: Teaser loans offer a low fixed rate in the early years and a higher rate later, creating future default risk for banks.

s: What is a Credit Default Swap?
o: A deposit insurance product with no counterparty exposure
A government grant to banks for purchasing government securities
An insurance-like derivative on bonds in which the seller pays upon default, with counterparty risk
A loan arrangement in which the borrower pays only after maturity
x: A Credit Default Swap is an insurance-like derivative on bonds; the seller pays when default occurs, and the contract carries counterparty risk.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a link in the sub-prime crisis chain described for its impact on India?
o: Securitisation into mortgage-backed securities sold worldwide
A rise in interest rates followed by home-loan defaults
A sustained fall in oil prices causing the banking collapse
x: The crisis chain involved weak borrowers, securitisation, rising rates, defaults and US bank failures. It was not caused by falling oil prices.

s: In the sub-prime crisis, into what were loans to weak borrowers securitised?
x: Sub-prime loans were securitised into mortgage-backed securities sold worldwide.

s: How did the Harshad Mehta scam (1992) move bank money into stocks?
x: The scam diverted bank funds into stocks via ready-forward G-Sec deals; infrastructure NBFC defaults describe IL&FS (2018).

s:
Consider the following statements about the PMC Bank failure:
1. The bank had hidden exposure to one realty group.
2. Dual control by the RBI and State Registrars weakened its oversight.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: PMC Bank hid its exposure to one realty group, and dual control by the RBI and State Registrars weakened oversight.

s: Which institution led the 2020 reconstruction of Yes Bank?
x: Yes Bank was placed under an RBI moratorium and rescued through an SBI-led reconstruction.

s: Who replaced Prashant Kumar as the CEO of Yes Bank in April 2026?
x: Prashant Kumar led Yes Bank from March 2020 after the SBI-led rescue; Vinay Tonse replaced him on 6 April 2026.

s: What did the PMC Bank failure of 2019 lead to?
x: PMC Bank's failure under dual control led to the BR (Amendment) Act, 2020.

s: Defaults at which institution triggered India's NBFC liquidity crisis of 2018?
x: Defaults by IL&FS, an infrastructure NBFC, triggered the 2018 NBFC liquidity crisis.

s: What does the term 'shadow banking' refer to?
o: Unauthorised branches of scheduled commercial banks
Financial activity of non-bank entities carried on outside regular bank regulation
Off-balance-sheet lending by the RBI to the government
Banking services provided only during non-working hours
x: Shadow banking means financial (credit) activity by non-bank entities such as NBFCs that lies outside regular bank regulation (UPPSC 2014 key). It is not about unauthorised bank branches, RBI lending to government, or banking hours.

s: What does asset-liability mismatch in the NBFC sector refer to?
o: Borrowing short-term funds and lending for long-term infrastructure or housing projects
Borrowing long and lending short exclusively in government securities
Holding only foreign currency assets against domestic liabilities
Matching every liability with an asset of identical maturity
x: NBFCs borrowed through short-term commercial paper and mutual fund money while lending for long-term infrastructure and housing, creating an asset-liability mismatch exposed by the IL&FS default.

s: Which of the following is a characteristic of NBFCs?
o: They can accept demand deposits and issue cheques as banks do.
They are registered under the Companies Act but cannot take demand deposits, issue cheques or join the payment system.
They are covered by DICGC irrespective of the type of deposit.
They are outside all forms of RBI regulation.
x: NBFCs are registered under the Companies Act and cannot take demand deposits, issue cheques or join the payment system; their deposits are not covered by DICGC.

s: The RBI's Scale-Based Regulation (October 2022) for NBFCs has Base, Middle and Upper layers. What is the fourth layer?
x: Scale-Based Regulation has Base, Middle, Upper and Top layers.

s: Which of the following is true of deposits with NBFCs in India?
o: Covered by DICGC up to ₹5 lakh
Covered by DICGC up to ₹1 lakh
x: NBFC deposits are not DICGC-covered; the ₹5 lakh cover applies to bank deposits.

s: The collapse of which currency marked the East Asian financial crisis of 1997?
x: The crisis involved the Thai baht collapse and short-term foreign debt; India's impact was limited by capital controls and low short-term debt.

s: Why did India suffer only limited harm in the 1997 East Asian crisis?
o: Capital controls and low short-term debt
x: Capital controls and low short-term debt limited India's harm; Basel III and FSDC came after the 2007-09 crisis.

s: The 'taper tantrum' of 2013, which hit the Indian rupee, was triggered by which of the following?
o: A rate cut by the European Central Bank
The US Federal Reserve signalling that it would taper its asset purchases
A devaluation of the Chinese yuan
x: In May 2013 the US Fed hinted it would slow its large-scale asset (bond) purchases, causing capital outflows from emerging markets like India.

s: By about how much did the rupee depreciate against the US dollar between the first US Fed tapering signal in May 2013 and 3 September 2013?
x: The RBI records a 17% fall of the rupee against the dollar, with about US$17 billion of reserves used, in that period.

s: What is the role of the FSDC in India's financial system?
x: The RBI regulates banks and NBFCs and IRDAI regulates insurers; the FSDC coordinates among financial regulators.

s: Who chairs the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC), set up in December 2010?
x: FSDC was set up in December 2010 and is chaired by the Union Finance Minister; it is not an organ of NITI Aayog.

s: The Financial Stability Report is published by the RBI with what periodicity?
o: Quarterly, in March, June, September and December
x: The RBI publishes the Financial Stability Report half-yearly, generally in June and December.

s: Who co-chaired the Committee on Financial Sector Assessment (CFSA) in India?
o: The Union Finance Minister and the RBI Governor
An RBI Deputy Governor and the Finance Secretary
The SEBI Chairperson and the Chief Economic Adviser
The RBI Governor and the NITI Aayog Vice-Chairperson
x: CFSA was co-chaired by an RBI Deputy Governor and the Finance Secretary (MPPSC 2020 key). The Finance Minister chairs FSDC and the RBI Governor chairs its sub-committee; SEBI, CEA and NITI Aayog did not co-chair CFSA.

s: Besides financial stability and development, what else does the FSDC focus on?
x: The FSDC covers financial stability and development and also financial literacy and inclusion.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)?
o: It is an organ of NITI Aayog
Its sub-committee is chaired by the RBI Governor
x: FSDC is not an organ of NITI Aayog; it handles macroprudential supervision and inter-regulatory coordination.

s: Who chairs the sub-committee of the FSDC?
x: The FSDC is chaired by the Finance Minister, but its sub-committee by the RBI Governor.

s: Which risk did the RBI's Financial Stability Report of June 2026 flag?
x: The half-yearly FSR of June 2026 flagged unsecured lending by fintechs as a risk.

s: What did the RBI's Financial Stability Report of December 2025 find?
o: Banks and NBFCs were resilient in stress tests
Several large banks breached minimum capital
NBFCs faced a liquidity crisis like IL&FS
